blocks.h2: What Does an Ejector Pump Do?
blocks.body: An ejector pump sits in a sealed basin under the basement floor. A basement toilet, shower, laundry or wet bar drains into it because those fixtures sit below the sewer line. When the basin fills, the pump pushes the wastewater up to the main line. In a home with an [overhead sewer system](/algonquin/overhead-sewer-systems), every basement drain goes through it.

blocks.h2: Ejector Pump Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: How do I know if I have an ejector pump?
items.preview: If you have a basement bathroom, look for a sealed lid in the floor.
items.answer: If your basement has a toilet, shower or laundry, look for a sealed lid in the floor with pipes and a vent. That's the basin.

items.q: What should I do when the alarm goes off?
items.preview: Stop using basement fixtures and call.
items.answer: Stop using everything that drains to the basin and keep the lid sealed. Then call us.

items.q: How long does an ejector pump last?
items.answer: Many last somewhere between 7 and 10 years or more. Wipes and grease shorten that.

items.q: Can wipes really ruin an ejector pump?
items.answer: Yes. Even flushable wipes wrap around the impeller and overload the motor. Only toilet paper should go down.

items.q: My basement bathroom smells like sewer. Is it the ejector?
items.preview: Often a lid seal or vent problem at the basin.
items.answer: Often. A worn lid gasket, a loose vent connection or a dry floor drain trap nearby can let sewer gas into the room. We check the basin and the vent first.

items.q: What does ejector pump replacement cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on the pump and basin. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, the basin, the check valve and venting and access. We quote a flat rate before we start.
